summary.text: 非 is an old graph whose early form has been interpreted as opposed wings or as two people back-to-back. Oracle-bone examples already use it as a negative, but the evidence does not show that this use developed from either proposed picture.

formation.text: The graph is best described as a disputed pictographic formation: one account sees wings facing away, while another reads two people back-to-back. The evidence does not settle the referent or establish an internal phonetic component. The selected Shang-style illustration is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

components.text: Treat the early graph as one whole picture. It has been interpreted as two wings facing away from each other or as two people back-to-back; the available graph evidence does not decide between these readings.

sound_limitation.text: The inspected analyses do not establish a phonetic component within 非’s own formation. Character readings therefore cannot supply a component-level sound comparison.

history.text: The received Shuowen explanation glosses 非 as opposition and interprets its form as the lower wings of 飛 facing away. This is an old explanation of the graph, not proof of its original referent or a dated route from that image to negation. A competing proposal reads early forms as two people back-to-back and relates 非 to 北; the accounts remain unresolved.

The selected Shang oracle-script-style illustration is a modern vector redraw associated with an identified Xiaoxuetang record, not an artifact photograph. Oracle-bone, bronze, bamboo/slip, and seal forms are reported, but their inventory does not establish a complete sequence of graphic changes.

uncertainties.text: The graph’s original referent remains unresolved: early forms have competing wing and human interpretations. The proposed relation to 北 is disputed, and the evidence does not settle whether 非 is related to 飛.

Oracle-bone examples already use 非 as a negative, but the evidence does not show whether negation developed from an earlier pictorial or opposition sense. A separate proposal that the spoken word 非 fuses 不 and 惟 is disputed; it does not mean the graph is composed of those characters.
No phonetic component within 非’s graphic formation is established in the inspected analyses, so no component-level sound comparison can be given.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 非 as a negative. Oracle-bone script is the earliest script class identified here, but the examples’ absolute dates are unresolved.

senses.period: Han-era dictionary explanation; earlier use unresolved
senses.text: The received Shuowen explanation gives 非 the sense ‘opposition’ and connects it with wings facing away. This is a historical interpretation, not proof that opposition was an earlier lexical stage.

senses.gloss: fault or wrongness; judging something wrong
senses.period: bronze inscriptions reported; absolute date unresolved
senses.text: Reported bronze examples use 非 for faults and for judging something wrong. Their chronological or semantic relation to the early negative use is unresolved.
Later dictionary records include uses meaning reproach or criticize. Their listing does not establish a complete chronology or a path from the negative sense.
A later dictionary records an ‘avoid’ sense, but its relation to the other senses is unresolved.
Modern references give negative meanings including ‘not’ and ‘non-’.

limitations.text: Early negative attestations do not establish whether the negative sense developed from a pictorial meaning or from opposition; no dated transition is supplied.
Reported uses for wrongness, reproach, and avoidance do not establish a complete chronology or the connections among those senses and negation.
The proposed 不 + 惟 fusion is a disputed account of the spoken word 非. It does not show that the graph was formed from 不 and 惟 or identify the name of a depicted object.

items.period: Shang oracle-script style; the modern file was uploaded in 2020
items.tradition: Oracle-bone script style; modern Inkscape vector redraw derived from Xiaoxuetang record 45.EC02, noted as 甲799 / 合34479
items.caption: This Shang oracle-script-style form of 非 is drawn as two opposed upright shapes with short strokes extending outward. Wang Qingju reads early forms as two people back-to-back, while another account interprets them as wings spread apart; the image alone does not resolve their origin.
items.alt: Black oracle-script-style glyph with two tall, opposed forms and short outward strokes, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: This is the sole supplied candidate and it provides a sourced illustration of an early form while allowing the competing interpretations to remain explicit.

limitations.text: The visible image is a modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. Its depicted shape does not establish whether 非 originated as people facing away or as wings; those are competing interpretations.
